sources.entry: docling - Library for converting documents into structured data.

summary.one_liner: Docling is a Python library that parses diverse document formats, including advanced PDF understanding, and converts them into a unified structured representation for generative AI use.
summary.what_it_does: Parses many document types (PDF, DOCX, PPTX, XLSX, HTML, EPUB, email, images, audio, video, LaTeX, plain text and more) into a unified DoclingDocument representation. Its PDF pipeline covers page layout, reading order, table structure, code, formulas and image classification. Output can be exported to Markdown, HTML, WebVTT, DocLang, DocTags and lossless JSON. It supports OCR for scanned PDFs and images, Visual Language Models such as GraniteDocling, and speech recognition for audio and video. It also offers a CLI, an MCP server, an API server (docling-serve), and integrations with LangChain, LlamaIndex, Crew AI and Haystack.
use_cases: convert PDFs to markdown for LLM input
transcribe audio or video into text
feed documents into RAG or agent pipelines
run document conversion offline on sensitive data
how_to_run: from docling.document_converter import DocumentConverter; result = DocumentConverter().convert(source); print(result.document.export_to_markdown())
notable: Unified DoclingDocument representation across many input formats
Local execution for sensitive data and air-gapped environments
Advanced PDF understanding including layout, reading order and table structure
Support for specialized XML schemas such as USPTO patents, JATS articles and XBRL financial reports
Chart understanding that converts charts into tables or code
caveats: Requires Python 3.10 or higher (Python 3.9 support dropped in 2.70.0)
Advanced features such as VLMs and ASR depend on additional models with their own licenses
README says metadata extraction and molecular structure understanding are still coming soon
